newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., council agrees to buy aquarium land.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., council agrees to buy aquarium land.

text.p: Florida's Tampa City Council signed off Thursday on an agreement to aquire the land the Florida Aquarium sits on, but refinancing of the $84 million aquarium bonds is still at least a month and a half away, city chief accountant Ron Ibarra said.
"We've got a lot of documents to prepare. We've got to get the land deal worked out," Ibarra said.
He estimated the council would give final approval on the bond refinancing "at the end of October, the first of November," with issuance following a few days later.
Merrill Lynch & Co is senior manager for the deal.
The struggling aquarium was built on port land with $84 million of revenue bonds issued by the city. The bonds were backed in part by a $10 million letter of credit from the Tampa Port Authority.

Attendance has been well below projections and the two-year-old aquarium is losing money even faster this year than in its first year of operation. It was forced to dip into reserves to make its $3.2 million debt service payment in May.
City officials projected the aquarium would exhaust reserve funds within two years.

As part of an agreement to refinance the bonds, the Port Authority agreed to give the city the aquarium land and to pay up to $166,912 a year for 10 years to cover revenue shortfalls. In exchange, the city would release the Port Authority from its letter of credit.
The Port Authority board signed off on the agreement on Monday and the city followed suit Thursday.
City officials have calculated that refinancing the bonds would save $43 million in debt service costs over 3O years.

The refinancing would restructure the debt, with initial debt service payments of about $4.3 million annually. Debt service would rise over the life of the bonds but would not exceed the current annual total of $7.2 million.
